correctness.rationale: Modulo a kernel subspace U, a lift of a fixed generator a≠1 of the projected cyclic subgroup is determined by its translation part (1-a)x, so the subgroup is uniquely determined by x+U and the projection order. For two such subgroups, any common nonidentity scalar can be lifted simultaneously iff x-y∈U+W; since 1-a is invertible for every nonidentity a, this permits either all of the common cyclic image or none of it. For eligible orders and fixed U,W with meet dimension r, a fixed first coset admits p^(dim(U+W)-dim W)=p^(k-r) second cosets, hence p^(n-r) pairs. The Gaussian expression counts U, the intersection in U, the quotient image of W, and graph maps from that image to U/(U∩W). For degree, restrict to r=0; fixing H leaves p^k conflicting cosets per eligible complement order for each disjoint W. This gives exactly Z, including the trivial subgroup. Subtract Z from B, then remove H and G, both distinct and meeting H nontrivially. The type exclusions cover all and only nonvertices; the ordered census includes the diagonal with correct multiplicity. Checks include kernel-only subgroups, coprime complement orders, and the full kernel dimension. For k=0 the degree simplifies to c(d) times the number of subspaces minus two, giving 18 and 28 in the p=7 example. The supporting enumeration is finite corroboration, inspected but not executed; the parametric proof is independent of it.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A diameter criterion does not determine the degree profile. A cyclic prime-power kernel has a chain of subgroups rather than a lattice of multidimensional subspaces. No truly stronger inspected statement counts how the complement lifts meet.

Nothing in the inspected degree, generation, diameter, or permutability statements already supplies it.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct result is the joint meet-order census with the associated full degree polynomial for faithful scalar action and rank at least two. Classical Gaussian subspace counting, diameter-two results, and intersection-graph definitions are not new. The closest inspected graph results change the group family, adjacency, or invariant and do not imply the joint census.
residual_risks: The primary 1969 and 2015 graph papers and the 2023 complementary-graph article could not be inspected in full. Ranked catalogue searches are not exhaustive. An earlier general lattice description together with published affine-flat intersection formulas could give closer coverage than the inspected sources.

value.rationale: This is a full local degree invariant of a standard graph on a natural semidirect-product family, backed by a more detailed meet-order distribution. It separates effects of intersecting subspaces from divisibility in the complement, so it identifies why distinct projection orders can create different graph degrees even at the same kernel dimension. It can be used to compare graphs or recover their edge census without enumerating the underlying subgroup lattice.
